hypothesis: Standard PyTorch F.kl_div computes KL divergence via cancellation-prone log-space subtraction, causing negative outputs in FP16/BF16/FP32 and backward gradient dead-zones/sign-flips under clamp(min=0) patches. We prove formal floating-point truncation and cancellation bounds for a two-branch 6th-order Bregman-Taylor identity with cancellation-free analytic gradients, benchmark our fused Blackwell Triton kernel against FP32-upcast, torch.compile (TorchInductor), Liger-style standard fused Triton, and chunked-FP32 up to V=151,936, and validate 3-seed BF16 SFT+KL and 200-step real RLHF policy optimization on Qwen3-1.7B (V=151,936) and SmolLM2-1.7B (V=49,152).
